name: ctrl-tab-recency-cycle
description: Ctrl-Tab and Ctrl-Shift-Tab walk tabs in most-recently-visited order, repeated presses walk deeper instead of toggling between two tabs, and a closed tab leaves the list instead of being walked to. Opens FOUR tabs in order (A, B, C, D - D ends up active), so the candidate list for a forward walk from D is exactly [C, B, A] - three real, distinct entries, matching the shape of the Rust unit test three_presses_reach_the_third_most_recent_tab_without_oscillating (which needs 3 candidates for its 3rd press to mean anything). The harness has a `key_hold_taps` action that presses Control ONCE, taps Tab three times under it, then releases Control ONCE - the held cycle Ctrl-Tab recency cycling actually depends on, which chaining three separate `key` actions (each releasing its own modifier) cannot express. The three held taps are graded by `recency_walk_distinct`, which reads the three 'target' ids straight out of the run log and checks they are pairwise distinct - not merely that three lines exist in order (vlog_after's limit, since grep has no cross-line backreference to compare captured VALUES). Phase 2 then closes the tab the walk committed to and checks a fresh single Ctrl-Tab still fires.

actions.note: let the sidebar render and the startup space's tab commit - this is tab A, already active
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot

cmd+t is permanently bound to openCommandBar, not new-tab. Accepting a palette match still opens a brand-new foreground tab through AtriumBrowserWindow::OpenCommandBarMatch (chrome::AddTabAt, unconditional) - this is the working method, copied from edit-focus-gate.json's proven cmd+l/type/return navigation, the only neighbour in this tree confirmed (VM-verified 2026-08-10) to land a wait_vlog on a tab it opened through the command bar.
gate: the palette actually opened before typing into it
a distinct fixture page from tab A's favicon-page.html, so tab B is distinguishable in the log by URL, not just by id
let autocomplete resolve a row for the typed URL, same timing edit-focus-gate.json measured as sufficient
commits the top match, which opens tab B as a new foreground tab and closes the palette - recency order is now B, A

PRECONDITION: proves tab B actually committed before anything below assumes a second tab exists. This is the check the previous fixture never had - four straight failed gate runs blamed the code for a setup that silently never happened.
same method for tab C
a third distinct fixture page, so tab C is distinguishable from both A and B in the log
commits the top match, which opens tab C as a new foreground tab and closes the palette - recency order is now C, B, A
PRECONDITION: proves tab C actually committed

same method for a FOURTH tab, D. Three tabs (A, B, C) only ever give a forward walk two real candidates (B, A) - not enough to tell 'walked deeper' apart from 'toggled', which is exactly the property that must be measured. D active makes the candidate list [C, B, A]: three real entries for three real presses.
a fourth distinct fixture page, so tab D is distinguishable from A, B and C
commits the top match, opening tab D as a new foreground tab - recency order is now D (active), C, B, A
PRECONDITION: proves tab D actually committed, giving four real tabs and a genuine 3-entry candidate list before the held cycle runs

the run that first shipped this scenario found Finder frontmost by this point (WARNING: about to send ctrl+tab x3 (held) but 'Finder' is frontmost) - opening a tab via the command bar closes a palette, which can hand focus back to Finder rather than Atrium. `activate` is idempotent and safe to repeat before every input burst, same as the one at the top of this scenario.

actions.vlog: Atrium: recency cycle step direction 1 target [0-9]+
actions.note: THE MEASURED PATH: Control pressed once, Tab tapped three times under it, Control released once - one cgevent process, so the modifier is never released between taps the way three separate `key` actions would release it. First tap must land on C, the previously-active tab (not D, the currently-active one). The SAME held walk must reach three DIFFERENT tabs (C, then B, then A) rather than oscillating between two - graded below by recency_walk_distinct reading the three target ids out of the log, not by ordering alone.
release commits the landed tab (A) to the front of the recency list and makes it active
re-assert focus before the next input burst, same reasoning as above

PHASE 2 SETUP: closes the tab the held walk just committed to (A) - cmd+w is not one of the rebound combos, so it is still stock IDC_CLOSE_TAB. Expects atrium::RecordTabRecencyClosed to remove A from the list the moment it observes the close.
re-assert focus before the next input burst, same reasoning as above
PHASE 2, THE CHECK: a fresh, single-press cycle after A's close still fires - proves the closed tab did not empty the candidate list (there are still two tabs left).
tab A gone from the strip and sidebar

assertions.label: tab-d-actually-created
assertions.desc: PRECONDITION: tab D committed, giving the held cycle a genuine 3-entry candidate list ([C, B, A]) to walk.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: recency cycle step direction 1 target [0-9]+
assertions.label: first-press-lands-on-previously-active-tab
assertions.desc: The held Ctrl-Tab sequence produced at least one recency-cycle step, proving the chord reached atrium::StepTabRecencyCycle rather than falling through to stock strip cycling. The ordering this used to check via after_pattern (a step after tab D committed) is now guaranteed by construction: d-page's eval_until action, earlier in this same action list, already blocks until D's own commit resolves, and key_hold_taps runs strictly after it.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: recency cycle step direction 1 target ([0-9]+)
assertions.label: three-held-taps-reach-three-distinct-tabs
assertions.desc: THE REAL END-TO-END EVIDENCE: reads the three 'target' ids the held key_hold_taps sequence produced and checks they are pairwise distinct. Unlike the old vlog_after-only check this replaces, this reads the CAPTURED VALUES, not just that three lines exist in order - a walk that toggled back to the same tab id on its third press would fail this even though three matching lines still exist. This is the scenario-level equivalent of the Rust unit test three_presses_reach_the_third_most_recent_tab_without_oscillating, now measured against a real held Control key sequence instead of resting on the Rust test alone. No after_pattern bound is needed: recency_walk_distinct only reads the FIRST `count` matches, and nothing before key_hold_taps ever emits this pattern, so the window is already exactly Phase 1's three steps.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: recency cycle step direction 1 target [0-9]+
assertions.label: phase2-fresh-cycle-fires
assertions.desc: A step that lands AFTER the cmd+w close, not merely somewhere in the log. As a bare vlog this passed off Phase 1's held taps and said nothing about Phase 2 - anchoring it on BrowserController::RemoveTab's 'tab N closed' is what makes it evidence that the post-close candidate list is still walkable.
Exactly one window throughout - recency cycling is a same-window navigation, never a new surface.
